Q: Best practice for serving shared HTML header/footer and extensionless URLs in static HTML A:

A) Generate your HTML with a static site generator

I join @furas's comment, by using a static site generator.

Personnaly, I'm very happy with 11ty (Eleventy), as it is easy to install, configure and extend. It is fast and handles a lot of different template engines, giving you a lot of flexibility. You'll also find some documentation and examples.

But depending on your background and favorite programming language, you could also use one of these:

  • Go: Hugo

  • PHP: Jigsaw or Sculpin

  • Python: Pelican or Lektor

  • Ruby: Jekyll

B) Use Server Side Includes (SSI) or Edge Side Includes (ESI)

And as you mentionned, another solution would be to use Server Side Includes, but it will be less flexible as you probably won't be able to host this anywhere. It is usually not active/installed on web servers by default, meaning that you'll probably have to do a custom setup.

Varnish is a very performant reverse proxy, which I used in the past for a big traffic website. The setup was a bit different as I had a CMS (Drupal) in the backend, but also some static files. The ESI can help you mix content in the same page, handling different cache lifetimes, as each fragment has its own TTL.

What are the best practices?

To answer your questions, I would say that doing rewrites rules in Apache or in NGINX is very common and a standard. Relying on a folder name being the URL and having always an index file in it is also common and has the little advantage of working by default without a server configuration. So choose what suits your best.

About the performance question, I would answer that serving static files will use less CPU, so will be slightly better. But the most important is how you serve your files, as many improvements can be done:

  • minify and aggregate your CSS and JS files. This can be done with a bundler before deploying. You'll certainly have one if you use a static site generator. If not, pick one of these: Vite, Turbopack, Rspack, esbuild, Rollup, etc.

  • compress your files with Brotli and/or GZip and serve them with a rewrite rule or enable a compression filter on the web server to do it on the fly. Don't forget to set the HTTP header Vary: Accept-Encoding as the response of the server will depend on what the browser can handle (which is sent via the Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br, zstd header).

  • set correct HTTP headers so that all your assets (css, js, images) can be stored in the cache of a reverse proxy, proxy and the browser's cache.
    Example: Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000.

    This will reduce a lot the number of requests to your server.

    Always add a version in your URL to the asset, so that you can easily update them and force a new version to be downloaded. This should also be done at build time.
    Example: ?v=3 or ?t=2026.08.03_10h15.

  • enable HTTP 2 or HTTP 3 if the server can do it.

Q: How to JOIN a column in codeigniter using a specific condition A:

Try this:

$this->db
  ->select('*')
  ->from('admins')
  ->join('profile', 'CONCAT("ABC", admins.admin_id, "U") = profile.identifier')
  ->where('email', $username)
  ->where('password', $password)
  ->where('status', 1);

Q: What's the difference between "call" and "invoke"? A:

Call usually means to execute something and wait for it to finish. You can directly execute a script, function, executable, or method. Invoke usually means triggering or requesting execution of something. In .NET you see method.Invoke() where you are invoking a method indirectly rather than calling it directly in code.
